It is conceivable that, for example, an identical hub to T-RICH could be built on the same-sized parcel directly to the north. Or, perhaps only additional storage tanks could be placed at one of these “satellite” parcels which would store CO liquefied at T-RICH. Several of the available parcels are already on deep water 2 channels, and there is currently a low, undeveloped area to the southwest that could be reclaimed and developed into an even larger hub site. No engineering work has yet been put into an estimate, but it would seem feasible that by connecting two or more of these sites together via pipelines or having them Page44 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version operate independently as nearly-identical hubs, the total CO throughput in this part of the port could 2 exceed 15 mtpa. Thus, as the volume of captured CO supplied by Florida industrial emitters increases, T- 2 RICH can be scaled up proportionately to accommodate this growth in the Florida CCS industry . Figure 3.19: Available Parcels (in dark blue) Within Short Radius of T-RICH Site. 3.10 LAND ACQUISITION PLAN As is typical with the nation’s ports, the local Port Authority owns the land and operators enter into long- term lease agreements in order to build on the land and operate a ship terminal, warehouse, and other cargo or vessel-related facilities. That is also the case with Port Tampa Bay, which owns, under a charter from the State of Florida, most of the land on which marine terminals are operating in the port. Accordingly, Aptamus expects to enter into a long term lease agreement, customarily for at least a 20- year term, in parallel with negotiations for CO supply and transportation commitments with customers 2 and partners. Port Tampa Bay’s website states that they will consider lease terms up to 40 years. Since PTB is a partner in this study and has confirmed that the chosen parcel can be used for this intended cargo operation, the primary remaining critical item is to ensure that the parcel remains available in the years it may take to solidify commercial agreements with CO “suppliers”. Aptamus is unlikely to commit 2 to a long-term tenant lease until it is highly confident that it will have a customer in place to supply CO 2 to the T-RICH hub for processing which would then be the cargo for its CO vessel for export out of Florida. 2 And this timeline depends on those potential future supply customers’ plans to study carbon capture, engage in pre-FEED and FEED studies, and then proceed into the formal EPC process. During the several years it may take for that process to play out, the risk is that the chosen parcel gets leased to another future tenant.
